newsitem.title: UK: Jury still out on Argos after Xmas slip.
newsitem.headline: Jury still out on Argos after Xmas slip.

text.p: British catalogue-based retailer Argos Plc needs to provide more evidence that its Christmas sales slowdown was a one-off before it can regain its star rating, retail analysts said.

The company, which warned in January that 1996 profits would be lower than expected because of weaker December sales, explained this was due to a drop in demand for toys, small electricals and jewellery - three of its key markets.
But analysts were not totally convinced.
"I didn't find the explanation that it was the market entirely satisfactory," said Victoria Melendez, retail analyst at Morgan Stanley.
The retailer, which reported a 14 percent increase in profits for 1996, said sales had picked up since Christmas and were seven percent ahead on a like for like basis.

Analysts were encouraged by this performance, but stressed the key question was whether this pace could be sustained into the second half. Some analysts said it would take more than one set of figures to reassure investors.
"The confidence knocked out of this stock (by the profit warning) will take longer to rebuild," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
He said he was cutting his 1997 forecast to 158 million stg from 160 million.
Other analysts said Argos's long term growth potential and underlying profit growth prospects weighed in its favour and the stock continued to deserve a premium rating.

They also said the new strategic planning role for Trevor Green, currently managing director of Argos Distributors, suggested acquisitions might be moving up the agenda. But others analysts said they did not expect anything in the near term.
The shares were up 11.5 pence at 650.5 by 1520 GMT. -- Jane Merriman, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
